CL:0000000.label: cell
CL:0000000.description: A material entity of anatomical origin (part of or deriving from an organism) that has as its parts a maximally connected cell compartment surrounded by a plasma membrane.

CL:0000540.label: neuron
CL:0000540.description: The basic cellular unit of nervous tissue. Each neuron consists of a body, an axon, and dendrites. Their purpose is to receive, conduct, and transmit impulses in the nervous system.

CL:0000101.label: sensory neuron
CL:0000101.description: Any neuron having a sensory function; an afferent neuron conveying sensory impulses.

CL:0000001.label: primary cultured cell
CL:0000001.description: A cultured cell that is freshly isolated from a organismal source, or derives in culture from such a cell prior to the culture being passaged.

CL:0000010.label: cultured cell
CL:0000010.description: A cell in vitro that is or has been maintained or propagated as part of a cell culture.

CL:0000002.label: obsolete immortal cell line cell
CL:0000002.description: OBSOLETE: A cell line cell that is expected to be capable of an unlimited number of divisions, and is thus able to support indefinite growth/propagation in vitro as part of a immortal cell line.
comments:
Obsoleted in July 2013 and replaced by the CLO 'immortal cell line cell' class, as a result of CLO-OBI-CL alignment efforts.

Covers cells actively being cultured or stored in a quiescent state for future use.

CL:0000003.label: obsolete native cell
CL:0000003.description: OBSOLETE. A cell that is found in a natural setting, which includes multicellular organism cells 'in vivo' (i.e. part of an organism), and unicellular organisms 'in environment' (i.e. part of a natural environment).

CL:0000004.label: obsolete cell by organism
CL:0000004.description: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by the organisms within which they are contained.
comments: This term was made obsolete because there is no difference in meaning between it and 'cell', as any cell can be classified by its species. If you have used this term in annotation, please replace it with cell (CL:0000000), native cell (CL:0000003), or cell in vitro (CL:0001034) as appropriate.

CL:0000005.label: neural crest derived fibroblast
CL:0000005.description: Any fibroblast that is derived from the neural crest.

CL:0000333.label: migratory neural crest cell
CL:0000333.description: A cell derived from the specialized ectoderm flanking each side of the embryonic neural plate, which after the closure of the neural tube, forms masses of cells that migrate out from the dorsal aspect of the neural tube to spread throughout the body.

CL:0000057.label: fibroblast
CL:0000057.description: A connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules. Flattened and irregular in outline with branching processes; appear fusiform or spindle-shaped.

CL:0000008.label: migratory cranial neural crest cell
CL:0000008.description: Cell that is part of the migratory cranial neural crest population. Migratory cranial neural crest cells develop from premigratory cranial neural crest cells and have undergone epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination.

CL:0000006.label: neuronal receptor cell
CL:0000006.description: Any sensory receptor cell that is a(n) neuron and is capable of some detection of stimulus involved in sensory perception.

CL:0000197.label: sensory receptor cell
CL:0000197.description: A cell that is capable of detection of a stimulus involved in sensory perception.

CL:0000007.label: early embryonic cell (metazoa)
CL:0000007.description: A cell found in the embryo before the formation of all the gem layers is complete.

CL:0000009.label: obsolete fusiform initial
CL:0000009.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000079 from Plant Ontology instead. An elongated cell with approximately wedge-shaped ends, found in the vascular cambium, which gives rise to the elements of the axial system in the secondary vascular tissues.

CL:0000578.label: experimentally modified cell in vitro
CL:0000578.description: A cell in vitro that has undergone physical changes as a consequence of a deliberate and specific experimental procedure.

CL:0000011.label: migratory trunk neural crest cell
CL:0000011.description: Cell that is part of the migratory trunk neural crest population. Migratory trunk neural crest cells develop from premigratory trunk neural crest cells and have undergone epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination.

CL:0000012.label: obsolete cell by class
comments: This term was made obsolete because there is no difference in meaning between it and 'cell', as any cell can be classified. If you have used this term in annotation, please replace it with cell (CL:0000000), native cell (CL:0000003), or cell in vitro (CL:0001034) as appropriate.

CL:0000014.label: germ line stem cell
CL:0000014.description: A stem cell that is the precursor of gametes.

CL:0000039.label: germ line cell
CL:0000039.description: A cell that is within the developmental lineage of gametes and is able to pass along its genetic material to offspring.

CL:0000034.label: stem cell
CL:0000034.description: A relatively undifferentiated cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

CL:0000015.label: male germ cell
CL:0000015.description: A germ cell that supports male gamete production. In some species, non-germ cells known as Sertoli cells also play a role in spermatogenesis.

CL:0000586.label: germ cell
CL:0000586.description: The reproductive cell in multicellular organisms.

CL:0000016.label: male germ line stem cell
CL:0000016.description: A stem cell that is the precursor of male gametes.

CL:0000017.label: spermatocyte
CL:0000017.description: A male germ cell that develops from spermatogonia. The euploid primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis and give rise to the haploid secondary spermatocytes which in turn give rise to spermatids.

CL:0000020.label: spermatogonium
CL:0000020.description: An euploid male germ cell of an early stage of spermatogenesis.

CL:0000018.label: spermatid
CL:0000018.description: A male germ cell that develops from the haploid secondary spermatocytes. Without further division, spermatids undergo structural changes and give rise to spermatozoa.

CL:0000255.label: eukaryotic cell
CL:0000255.description: Any cell that in taxon some Eukaryota.

CL:0000413.label: haploid cell
CL:0000413.description: A cell whose nucleus contains a single haploid genome.

CL:0000657.label: secondary spermatocyte
CL:0000657.description: One of the two haploid cells into which a primary spermatocyte divides, and which in turn gives origin to spermatids.

CL:0000019.label: sperm
CL:0000019.description: A mature male germ cell that develops from a spermatid.

CL:0000408.label: male gamete
CL:0000408.description: Any male germ cell that has characteristic some haploid and is capable of some fertilization.

CL:0000021.label: female germ cell
CL:0000021.description: Female germ cell is a germ cell that supports female gamete production.

CL:0000022.label: female germ line stem cell
CL:0000022.description: A stem cell that is the precursor of female gametes.

CL:0000023.label: oocyte
CL:0000023.description: A female germ cell that has entered meiosis.

CL:0000024.label: oogonial cell
CL:0000024.description: An undifferentiated germ cell that proliferates rapidly and gives rise to oocytes.

CL:0000670.label: primordial germ cell
CL:0000670.description: A primordial germ cell is a diploid germ cell precursors that transiently exist in the embryo before they enter into close association with the somatic cells of the gonad and become irreversibly committed as germ cells.

CL:0000025.label: egg cell
CL:0000025.description: A female gamete where meiosis has progressed to metaphase II and is able to participate in fertilization.

CL:0000675.label: female gamete
CL:0000675.description: A mature sexual reproductive cell of the female germline.

CL:0000026.label: invertebrate nurse cell
CL:0000026.description: A germline cell that contributes to the development of the oocyte by transferring cytoplasm directly to oocyte.

CL:0000412.label: polyploid cell
CL:0000412.description: A cell that contains more than two haploid sets of chromosomes.

CL:4029002.label: germline-derived nurse cell
CL:4029002.description: A gamete-nursing cell that derives from a germline cell (del Pino, 2021).

CL:0000027.label: smooth muscle cell neural crest derived
CL:0000027.description: A smooth muscle cell derived from the neural crest.

CL:0000192.label: smooth muscle cell
CL:0000192.description: A non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. They develop from specialized myoblasts (smooth muscle myoblast).

CL:2000029.label: central nervous system neuron
CL:2000029.description: Any neuron that is part of a central nervous system.

CL:0000338.label: neuroblast (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
CL:0000338.description: A neural precursor of the central nervous system.

CL:0000029.label: neural crest derived neuron
CL:0000029.description: Any neuron that develops from some migratory neural crest cell.

CL:0002676.label: neural crest derived neuroblast
CL:0002676.description: A neuroblast derived from a neural crest cell.

CL:0000030.label: glioblast
CL:0000030.description: A non-terminally differentiated cell that develops form the neuroectoderm. Glioblast has the potential to differentiate into various types of glial cells, including astrocytes and oligodendrocytes.

CL:0011026.label: progenitor cell
CL:0011026.description: A precursor cell that has a tendency to differentiate into a specific type of cell. They are descendants of stem cells, only they are more constrained in their differentiation potential or capacity for self-renewal, and are often more limited in both senses.

CL:0000133.label: neurectodermal cell
CL:0000133.description: Ectoderm destined to be nervous tissue.

CL:0000031.label: neuroblast (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000031.description: A cell that will develop into a neuron often after a migration phase.

CL:0000032.label: neuroplacodal cell
CL:0000032.description: A cell of a platelike structure, especially a thickened plate of ectoderm in the early embryo, from which a sense organ develops.

CL:0000114.label: surface ectodermal cell
CL:0000114.description: An ectodermal cell that is part of the external ectoderm, forming the outermost layer of the developing embryo. It is characterized by its polarized nature, with distinct apical and basal surfaces (Ferrante Jr., Reinke, & Stanley, 1995). Surface ectodermal cell gives rise to the epidermis, hair follicles, nails, sensory organs, and specialized structures like the apical ectodermal ridge crucial for limb development (Skoufa et al., 2024).

CL:0000033.label: apocrine cell
CL:0000033.description: An exocrine cell characterized by loss of part of the cytoplasm during the process of secretion. The secreted substance is accumulated at the apical end and is either budded off through the plasma membrane producing secreted vesicles or dissolved in the cytoplasm that is lost during secretion.

CL:0000152.label: exocrine cell
CL:0000152.description: A cell of an exocrine gland; i.e. a gland that discharges its secretion via a duct.

CL:0011115.label: precursor cell
CL:0011115.description: A cell that, by division or terminal differentiation, can give rise to other cell types.

CL:0000035.label: single fate stem cell
CL:0000035.description: A stem cell that self-renews as well as give rise to a single mature cell type.

CL:0000723.label: somatic stem cell
CL:0000723.description: A stem cell that can give rise to cell types of the body other than those of the germ-line.

CL:0000036.label: epithelial fate stem cell
CL:0000036.description: A somatic stem cell that is committed to an epithelial fate, possessing the capacity for self-renewal and the ability to differentiate into one or more distinct mature cell types of the epithelial lineage. This cell is crucial for the development, homeostasis, repair, and regeneration of epithelial tissues.

CL:0000037.label: hematopoietic stem cell
CL:0000037.description: A stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop, including blood cells and cells of the immune system. Hematopoietic stem cells lack cell markers of effector cells (lin-negative). Lin-negative is defined by lacking one or more of the following cell surface markers: CD2, CD3 epsilon, CD4, CD5 ,CD8 alpha chain, CD11b, CD14, CD19, CD20, CD56, ly6G, ter119.

CL:0000988.label: hematopoietic cell
CL:0000988.description: A cell of a hematopoietic lineage.

CL:0008001.label: hematopoietic precursor cell
CL:0008001.description: Any hematopoietic cell that is a precursor of some other hematopoietic cell type.

CL:0000566.label: angioblastic mesenchymal cell
CL:0000566.description: A mesenchymal stem cell capable of developing into blood vessel endothelium.

CL:0000038.label: erythroid progenitor cell
CL:0000038.description: A progenitor cell committed to the erythroid lineage.

CL:0000764.label: erythroid lineage cell
CL:0000764.description: A immature or mature cell in the lineage leading to and including erythrocytes.

CL:0000839.label: myeloid lineage restricted progenitor cell
CL:0000839.description: A progenitor cell restricted to the myeloid lineage.

CL:0000050.label: megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor cell
CL:0000050.description: A progenitor cell committed to the megakaryocyte and erythroid lineages.

CL:0000040.label: monoblast
CL:0000040.description: A myeloid progenitor cell committed to the monocyte lineage. This cell is CD11b-positive, has basophilic cytoplasm, euchromatin, and the presence of a nucleolus.

CL:0017503.label: basophilic cytoplasm
CL:0017503.description: Cytoplasm that exhibits molecular interaction for basic dyes under specific pH conditions.

CL:0002194.label: monopoietic cell
CL:0002194.description: A cell involved in the formation of a monocyte (monopoiesis).

CL:0000763.label: myeloid cell
CL:0000763.description: A cell of the monocyte, granulocyte, mast cell, megakaryocyte, or erythroid lineage.

CL:0002009.label: macrophage dendritic cell progenitor
CL:0002009.description: A progenitor cell that can give rise to plasmacytoid and myeloid dendritic cells, and to monocytes and macrophages.

CL:0000041.label: mature eosinophil
CL:0000041.description: A fully differentiated eosinophil, a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and which can be stained by the dye eosin. Cells are also differentiated from other granulocytes by a small nuclear-to-cytoplasm ratio (1:3). This cell type is CD49d-positive.

CL:0000771.label: eosinophil
CL:0000771.description: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and which can be stained by the dye eosin. Eosinophils are CD9-positive, CD191-positive, and CD193-positive.

CL:0000145.label: professional antigen presenting cell
CL:0000145.description: A cell capable of processing and presenting lipid and protein antigens to T cells in order to initiate an immune response.

CL:0000774.label: band form eosinophil
CL:0000774.description: A late eosinophilic metamyelocyte in which the nucleus is in the form of a curved or coiled band, not having acquired the typical multilobar shape of the mature eosinophil.

CL:0000042.label: neutrophilic myeloblast
CL:0000042.description: A myeloblast committed to the neutrophil lineage. This cell type is GATA-1 positive, C/EBPa-positive, AML-1-positive, c-myb-positive and has low expression of PU.1 transcription factor.

CL:0000835.label: myeloblast
CL:0000835.description: The most primitive precursor in the granulocytic series, having fine, evenly distributed chromatin, several nucleoli, a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ration (5:1-7:1), and a nongranular basophilic cytoplasm. They reside in the bone marrow.

CL:0000834.label: neutrophil progenitor cell
CL:0000834.description: A progenitor cell of the neutrophil lineage.

CL:0000043.label: mature basophil
CL:0000043.description: A fully differentiated basophil, a granular leukocyte with an irregularly shaped, pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm that contains coarse granules of variable size. Basophils contain vasoactive amines such as histamine and serotonin, which are released on appropriate stimulation.

CL:0000767.label: basophil
CL:0000767.description: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has an irregularly shaped, pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm that contains coarse, bluish-black granules of variable size. Basophils contain vasoactive amines such as histamine and serotonin, which are released on appropriate stimulation. A basophil is CD123-positive, CD193-positive, CD203c-positive, and FceRIa-positive.

CL:0002274.label: histamine secreting cell
CL:0002274.description: A cell type that secretes histamine.

CL:0000770.label: band form basophil
CL:0000770.description: A late basophilic metamyelocyte in which the nucleus is in the form of a curved or coiled band, not having acquired the typical multilobar shape of the mature basophil.

CL:0000051.label: common lymphoid progenitor
CL:0000051.description: A oligopotent progenitor cell committed to the lymphoid lineage.

CL:0000045.label: obsolete thymus processed stem cell
CL:0000045.description: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).
comments: Consider using term 'pro-T cell ; CL:0000827' or the term 'thymocyte ; CL:0000893' or one of its children instead.

CL:0000046.label: obsolete bursa processed stem cell
CL:0000046.description: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).
comments: Consider using term 'pro-B cell ; CL:0000826' or the term 'immature B cell ; CL:0000816 or one of its children instead.

CL:0000047.label: neural stem cell
CL:0000047.description: An undifferentiated neural cell that originates from the neuroectoderm and has the capacity both to perpetually self-renew without differentiating and to generate multiple central nervous system neuronal and glial cell types.

CL:0002319.label: neural cell
CL:0002319.description: A cell that is part of the nervous system.

CL:0000048.label: multi fate stem cell
CL:0000048.description: A stem cell that can give rise to multiple lineages of cells.

CL:0000049.label: common myeloid progenitor
CL:0000049.description: A progenitor cell committed to myeloid lineage, including the megakaryocyte and erythroid lineages.

CL:0002032.label: hematopoietic oligopotent progenitor cell
CL:0002032.description: A hematopoietic oligopotent progenitor cell that has the ability to differentiate into limited cell types but lacks lineage cell markers and self renewal capabilities.

CL:0000557.label: granulocyte monocyte progenitor cell
CL:0000557.description: A hematopoietic progenitor cell that is committed to the granulocyte and monocyte lineages. These cells are CD123-positive, and do not express Gata1 or Gata2 but do express C/EBPa, and Pu.1.

CL:0000052.label: totipotent stem cell
CL:0000052.description: A stem cell from which all cells of the body can form.

CL:0000059.label: ameloblast
CL:0000059.description: Skeletogenic cell that produces enamel, overlies the odontogenic papilla, and arises from the differentiation of a preameloblast cell.

CL:0000054.label: obsolete bone matrix secreting cell
comments: synonymous with 'osteoblast'

CL:0000062.label: osteoblast
CL:0000062.description: Skeletogenic cell that secretes osteoid, is capable of producing mineralized (hydroxyapatite) matrix, is located adjacent to or within osteoid tissue, and arises from the transformation of a preosteoblast cell.

CL:0000055.label: obsolete non-terminally differentiated cell
CL:0000055.description: OBSOLETE. A precursor cell with a limited number of potential fates.
comments: Redundant grouping term
define using PATO mulit-potent or oligopotent?

CL:0000056.label: myoblast
CL:0000056.description: A cell that is commited to differentiating into a muscle cell.  Embryonic myoblasts develop from the mesoderm. They undergo proliferation, migrate to their various sites, and then differentiate into the appropriate form of myocytes.  Myoblasts also occur as transient populations of cells in muscles undergoing repair.

CL:0000680.label: muscle precursor cell
CL:0000680.description: A non-terminally differentiated cell that is capable of developing into a muscle cell.

CL:0000499.label: stromal cell
CL:0000499.description: A connective tissue cell of an organ found in the loose connective tissue.

CL:0000058.label: chondroblast
CL:0000058.description: Skeletogenic cell that is typically non-terminally differentiated, secretes an avascular, GAG rich matrix; is not buried in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, located adjacent to cartilage tissue (including within the perichondrium), and develops from prechondroblast (and thus prechondrogenic) cell.

CL:0002320.label: connective tissue cell
CL:0002320.description: A cell of the supporting or framework tissue of the body, arising chiefly from the embryonic mesoderm and including adipose tissue, cartilage, and bone.

CL:0007009.label: prechondroblast
CL:0007009.description: Skeletogenic cell that has the potential to develop into a chondroblast; and arises from neural crest, meseosdermal and notochordal and connective tissue cells.

CL:0002077.label: ecto-epithelial cell
CL:0002077.description: An epithelial cell derived from ectoderm.

CL:1100001.label: secretory epithelial cell
CL:1100001.description: An epithelial cell that is specialised for the synthesis and secretion of specific biomolecules.

CL:0007000.label: preameloblast
CL:0007000.description: Skeletogenic cell that has the potential to develop into an ameloblast. Located in the inner enamel epithelium, these cells elongate, their nuclei shift distally (away from the dental papilla), and their cytoplasm becomes filled with organelles needed for synthesis and secretion of enamel proteins.

CL:0000060.label: odontoblast
CL:0000060.description: Skeletogenic cell that secretes dentine matrix, is derived from the odontogenic papilla, and develops from a preodontoblast cell.

CL:0000710.label: neurecto-epithelial cell
CL:0000710.description: Epithelial cells derived from neural plate and neural crest.

CL:0002148.label: dental pulp cell
CL:0002148.description: A cell found within the dental pulp.

CL:0007003.label: preodontoblast
CL:0007003.description: Skeletogenic cell that has the potential to form an odontoblast, deposits predentine, and arises from a cranial neural crest cell.

CL:0000061.label: cementoblast
CL:0000061.description: Skeletogenic cell that produces cementum (a bony substance that covers the root of a tooth), is part of the odontogenic papilla, and develops from a precementoblast cell.

CL:0000151.label: secretory cell
CL:0000151.description: A cell that specializes in controlled release of one or more substances.

CL:0007002.label: precementoblast
CL:0007002.description: Skeletogenic cell that has the potential to develop into a cementoblast.

CL:0007010.label: preosteoblast
CL:0007010.description: Skeletogenic cell that has the potential to transform into an osteoblast, and develops from neural crest or mesodermal cells.

CL:0000063.label: obsolete cell by histology
CL:0000063.description: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by their microscopic appearance.
comments: This term was made obsolete because there is no difference in meaning between it and 'cell', as any cell can be classified by its microscopic appearance. If you have used this term in annotation, please replace it with cell (CL:0000000), native cell (CL:0000003), or cell in vitro (CL:0001034) as appropriate.

CL:0000064.label: ciliated cell
CL:0000064.description: A cell that has a filiform extrusion of the cell surface.

CL:0000065.label: ependymal cell
CL:0000065.description: A neuroepithelial glial cell, derived from a radial glial cell originating from the neuroectoderm, lines the ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord. This cell is characterized by the presence of cilia on its apical surface, which can be motile or non-motile.

CL:0000066.label: epithelial cell
CL:0000066.description: A cell that is usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface. The cell has a cytoskeleton that allows for tight cell to cell contact and for cell polarity where apical part is directed towards the lumen and the basal part to the basal lamina.

CL:0000067.label: ciliated epithelial cell
CL:0000067.description: An epithelial cell that has a cilia.

CL:0000125.label: glial cell
CL:0000125.description: A non-neuronal cell of the nervous system. They not only provide physical support, but also respond to injury, regulate the ionic and chemical composition of the extracellular milieu. Guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons.

CL:0000681.label: radial glial cell
CL:0000681.description: A cell present in the developing CNS. Functions as both a precursor cell and as a scaffold to support neuronal migration.

CL:0000738.label: leukocyte
CL:0000738.description: An achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages capable of ameboid movement, found in blood or other tissue.

CL:0000068.label: duct epithelial cell
CL:0000068.description: An epithelial cell that is part of a duct.

CL:0000071.label: blood vessel endothelial cell
CL:0000071.description: An endothelial cell that lines the vasculature.

CL:0000115.label: endothelial cell
CL:0000115.description: An endothelial cell comprises the outermost layer or lining of anatomical structures and can be squamous or cuboidal. In mammals, endothelial cell has vimentin filaments and is derived from the mesoderm.

CL:0002139.label: endothelial cell of vascular tree
CL:0002139.description: An endothelial cell of the vascular tree, which includes blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.

CL:0002078.label: meso-epithelial cell
CL:0002078.description: Epithelial cell derived from mesoderm or mesenchyme.

CL:0000215.label: obsolete barrier cell
CL:0000215.description: OBSOLETE. A cell whose primary function is to prevent the transport of stuff across compartments.
comments: Not needed term

CL:0000074.label: obsolete epithem cell
CL:0000074.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000066 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell that constitutes the mesophyll of a hydathode and is located between the xylem endings and the epidermis. Proposed to be involved in the retrieval of solutes from the xylem sap.

CL:0000075.label: columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell
CL:0000075.description: A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface. Columnar/cuboidal epithelial cells take on the shape of a column or cube.

CL:0000077.label: mesothelial cell
CL:0000077.description: A flat, squamous-like epithelial cell of mesodermal origin. It forms the mesothelium, which lines the body's serous cavities including the pleural, peritoneal, and pericardial spaces. This cell plays a crucial role in synthesizing and secreting lubricants, such as glycosaminoglycans and surfactants, which minimize friction between adjacent tissues during movement.

CL:0000078.label: peridermal cell
CL:0000078.description: Any squamous epithelial cell that is part of some periderm.

CL:0000362.label: epidermal cell
CL:0000362.description: An epithelial cell of the integument (the outer layer of an organism).

CL:0000079.label: stratified epithelial cell
CL:0000079.description: An epithelial cell, organized into multiple layers, with only the basal layer being in contact with the basement membrane.

CL:0000080.label: circulating cell
CL:0000080.description: A cell which moves among different tissues of the body, via blood, lymph, or other medium.

CL:0000081.label: blood cell
CL:0000081.description: A cell found predominately in the blood.

CL:0000082.label: epithelial cell of lung
CL:0000082.description: An epithelial cell of the lung.

CL:0002632.label: epithelial cell of lower respiratory tract
CL:0002632.description: Any epithelial cell that is part of some lower respiratory tract epithelium.

CL:0000083.label: epithelial cell of pancreas
CL:0000083.description: An epithelial cell of the pancreas.

CL:0002076.label: endo-epithelial cell
CL:0002076.description: An epithelial cell derived from endoderm.

CL:0000084.label: T cell
CL:0000084.description: A type of lymphocyte whose defining characteristic is the expression of a T cell receptor complex.

CL:0000542.label: lymphocyte
CL:0000542.description: A lymphocyte is a leukocyte commonly found in the blood and lymph that has the characteristics of a large nucleus, a neutral staining cytoplasm, and prominent heterochromatin.

CL:0000827.label: pro-T cell
CL:0000827.description: A lymphoid progenitor cell of the T cell lineage, with some lineage specific marker expression, but not yet fully committed to the T cell lineage.

CL:0000945.label: lymphocyte of B lineage
CL:0000945.description: A lymphocyte of B lineage with the commitment to express an immunoglobulin complex.

CL:0000085.label: obsolete germ line stem cell (sensu Vertebrata)
comments: Obsoleted as there is no need for a term specific for vertebrates.

CL:0000086.label: obsolete germ line stem cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
comments: Obsoleted as there is no need for a term specific for nematods and protostomes.

CL:0000087.label: obsolete male germ line stem cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
comments: Obsoleted as there is no need for a term specific for nematods and protostomes.

CL:0000088.label: obsolete female germ line stem cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
comments: Obsoleted as there is no need for a term specific for nematods and protostomes.

CL:0000089.label: obsolete male germ line stem cell (sensu Vertebrata)
comments: Obsoleted as there is no need for a term specific for vertebrates.

CL:0000090.label: obsolete female germ line stem cell (sensu Vertebrata)
comments: Obsoleted as there is no need for a term specific for vertebrates.

CL:0000091.label: Kupffer cell
CL:0000091.description: A tissue-resident macrophage of the reticuloendothelial system found on the luminal surface of the hepatic sinusoids involved in erythrocyte clearance. Markers include F4/80+, CD11b-low, CD68-positive, sialoadhesin-positive, CD163/SRCR-positive. Irregular, with long processes including lamellipodia extending into the sinusoid lumen, have flattened nucleus with cytoplasm containing characteristic invaginations of the plasma membrane (vermiform bodies); lie within the sinusoid lumen attached to the endothelial surface; derived from the bone marrow, form a major part of the body's mononuclear phagocyte system.

CL:0000864.label: tissue-resident macrophage
CL:0000864.description: A macrophage constitutively resident in a particular tissue under non-inflammatory conditions, and capable of phagocytosing a variety of extracellular particulate material, including immune complexes, microorganisms, and dead cells.

CL:0000092.label: osteoclast
CL:0000092.description: A specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue, which typically differentiates from monocytes. This cell has the following markers: tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase type 5-positive, PU.1-positive, c-fos-positive, nuclear factor NF-kappa-B p100 subunit-positive, tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 11A-positive and macrophage colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor-positive.

CL:0000766.label: myeloid leukocyte
CL:0000766.description: A cell of the monocyte, granulocyte, or mast cell lineage.

CL:0000518.label: phagocyte (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000518.description: A phagocyte in vertebrates that is able to phagocytosis.

CL:0001035.label: bone cell
CL:0001035.description: A connective tissue cell found in bone.

CL:0000576.label: monocyte
CL:0000576.description: Myeloid mononuclear recirculating leukocyte that can act as a precursor of tissue macrophages, osteoclasts and some populations of tissue dendritic cells.

CL:0000093.label: obsolete osteochondroclast
CL:0000093.description: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).
comments: Consider using 'osteoclast ; CL:0000092' instead.

CL:0000094.label: granulocyte
CL:0000094.description: A leukocyte with abundant granules in the cytoplasm.

CL:0000096.label: mature neutrophil
CL:0000096.description: A fully differentiated neutrophil, a granular leukocyte having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes. They are produced in bone marrow at a rate of 5e10-10e10/day and have a half-life of 6-8 hours. Neutrophils are CD15-positive, CD16-positive, CD32-positive, CD43-positive, CD181-positive, and CD182-positive.

CL:0017500.label: neutrophillic cytoplasm
CL:0017500.description: Cytoplasm that exhibits a characteristic staining and color, pale-pink, with Wright-Giemsa stain.

CL:0000775.label: neutrophil
CL:0000775.description: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.

CL:0000234.label: phagocyte
CL:0000234.description: Any cell capable of ingesting particulate matter via phagocytosis.

CL:0000097.label: mast cell
CL:0000097.description: A cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation. Progenitors leave bone marrow and mature in connective and mucosal tissue. Mature mast cells are found in all tissues, except the bloodstream. Their phenotype is CD117-high, CD123-negative, CD193-positive, CD200R3-positive, and FceRI-high. Stem-cell factor (KIT-ligand; SCF) is the main controlling signal of their survival and development.

CL:0000831.label: mast cell progenitor
CL:0000831.description: A progenitor cell of the mast cell lineage. Markers for this cell are FceRIa-low, CD117-positive, CD9-positive, T1/ST2-positive, SCA1-negative, and lineage-negative.

CL:0000098.label: sensory epithelial cell
CL:0000098.description: A specialized epithelial cell involved in sensory perception. Restricted to special sense organs of the olfactory, gustatory, and vestibulocochlear receptor systems; contain sensory cells surrounded by supportive, non-receptive cells.

CL:0000099.label: interneuron
CL:0000099.description: Most generally any neuron which is not motor or sensory. Interneurons may also refer to neurons whose axons remain within a particular brain region as contrasted with projection neurons which have axons projecting to other brain regions.

CL:0000100.label: motor neuron
CL:0000100.description: An efferent neuron that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes or inhibits movement.

CL:0000527.label: efferent neuron
CL:0000527.description: A neuron which sends impulses peripherally to activate muscles or secretory cells.

CL:0000526.label: afferent neuron
CL:0000526.description: A neuron which conveys sensory information centrally from the periphery.

CL:0000102.label: polymodal neuron
CL:0000102.description: A neuron type that respond to multiple stimuli such as mechanical, thermal and chemical. This neuron type is responsible for integrating different types of sensory inputs, allowing organisms to respond appropriately to diverse environmental challenges.

CL:2000032.label: peripheral nervous system neuron
CL:2000032.description: A neuron that is part of a peripheral nervous system.

CL:0000103.label: bipolar neuron
CL:0000103.description: A type of interneuron that has two neurites, usually an axon and a dendrite, extending from opposite poles of an ovoid cell body.

CL:0000104.label: multipolar neuron
CL:0000104.description: A neuron with three or more neurites, usually an axon and multiple dendrites.

CL:0000105.label: pseudounipolar neuron
CL:0000105.description: Neuron with two neurites that are fused grossly when they protrude from the soma and bifurcate a short distance from the soma.

CL:0000106.label: unipolar neuron
CL:0000106.description: Neuron with one neurite that extends from the cell body.

CL:0000107.label: autonomic neuron
CL:0000107.description: A neuron whose cell body is within an autonomic ganglion.

CL:0000108.label: cholinergic neuron
CL:0000108.description: A neuron that uses acetylcholine as a vesicular neurotransmitter.

CL:4033050.label: catecholaminergic neuron
CL:4033050.description: A neuron that releases catecholamine as a neurotransmitter.

CL:0000110.label: peptidergic neuron
CL:0000110.description: A neuron that uses neuropeptides as transmitters.

CL:0000111.label: obsolete peripheral neuron
CL:0000111.description: OBSOLETE A neuron that is part of nerve found outside the central nervous system.
comments: Merging into CL:2000032.

CL:0000112.label: columnar neuron
CL:0000112.description: A neuron of the invertebrate central nervous system. This neuron innervates the central complex (CX) of an invertebrate brain and it forms columnar patterns with its dendrites. It is involved in navigation and spatial processing.

CL:0008028.label: visual system neuron
CL:0008028.description: Any neuron that is capable of part of some visual perception.

CL:0000113.label: mononuclear phagocyte
CL:0000113.description: A vertebrate phagocyte with a single nucleus.

CL:0000842.label: mononuclear leukocyte
CL:0000842.description: A leukocyte with a single non-segmented nucleus in the mature form.

CL:0000221.label: ectodermal cell
CL:0000221.description: A cell of the outer of the three germ layers of the embryo.

CL:0000222.label: mesodermal cell
CL:0000222.description: A cell of the middle germ layer of the embryo.

CL:0000116.label: pioneer neuron
CL:0000116.description: Pioneer neurons establish a pathway in the developing central nervous system and then undergo programmed cell death once the adult axons, which follow them, have made connections with the target site. Thus, they are a transient cell type involved in axon guidance.

CL:0000118.label: basket cell
CL:0000118.description: Basket cells are inhibitory GABAergic interneurons of the brain. In general, dendrites of basket cells are free branching and contain smooth spines. Axons are highly branched. The branched axonal arborizations give rise to basket-like structures that surround the soma of the target cell. Basket cells form axo-somatic synapses, meaning their synapses target somas of other cells.

CL:0011005.label: GABAergic interneuron
CL:0011005.description: An interneuron that uses GABA as a vesicular neurotransmitter.  These interneurons are inhibitory

CL:0000119.label: cerebellar Golgi cell
CL:0000119.description: Large intrinsic neuron located in the granule layer of the cerebellar cortex that extends its dendrites into the molecular layer where they receive contact from parallel fibers. The axon of the Golgi cell ramifies densely in the granule layer and enters into a complex arrangement with mossy fiber terminals and granule cell dendrites to form the cerebellar glomerulus. Llinas, Walton and Lang. In The Synaptic Organization of the Brain. 5th ed. 2004.

CL:4023057.label: cerebellar inhibitory GABAergic interneuron
CL:4023057.description: Any GABAergic interneuron that has its soma located in some cerebellar cortex.

CL:0000120.label: granule cell
CL:0000120.description: A neuron of the vertebrate central nervous system that is small in size. This general class includes small neurons in the granular layer of the cerebellar cortex, cerebral cortex neurons that are not pyramidal cells and small neurons without axons found in the olfactory bulb.

CL:0000121.label: Purkinje cell
CL:0000121.description: An inhibitory neuron and the sole output neuron of the cerebellar cortex, the Purkinje cell's soma is located between the granular and molecular layers of the cerebellum. It is one of the largest neural cells in the mammalian brain, ranging from 50 to 80 micrometres in diameter. Purkinje cells have planar, fan-shaped dendrites that branch extensively with little overlap. This cell type receives synaptic input from parallel fibres, which modulate high-frequency spike activity known as "simple spikes," and climbing fibres, which modulate infrequent calcium spike activity known as "complex spikes". Purkinje cells are involved in motor coordination, particularly in correcting movements in progress.

CL:0000617.label: GABAergic neuron
CL:0000617.description: A neuron that uses GABA as a vesicular neurotransmitter

CL:0000122.label: stellate neuron
CL:0000122.description: A neuron that has dendritic processes radiating from the cell body forming a star-like shape.

CL:0000124.label: obsolete glial cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
comments: This is a grouping class that is no longer needed or wanted.

CL:0000126.label: macroglial cell
CL:0000126.description: A neuroglial cell of ectodermal origin, i.e., the astrocytes and oligodendrocytes considered together.

CL:0000339.label: glioblast (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000339.description: An early neural cell developing from the early ependymal cell of the neural tube.

CL:0000127.label: astrocyte
CL:0000127.description: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes (from 'star' cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with 'end feet' which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and 'reactive astrocytes' (along with microglia) respond to injury.

CL:0000128.label: oligodendrocyte
CL:0000128.description: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system. Form the insulating myelin sheath of axons in the central nervous system.

CL:4023154.label: myelinating glial cell
CL:4023154.description: A glial cell that myelinates axonal processes.

CL:0002453.label: oligodendrocyte precursor cell
CL:0002453.description: A proliferative and migratory glial progenitor cell that derives from a neural stem cell and resides within the central nervous system. It possesses the capacity to differentiate into a committed oligodendrocyte progenitor (COP) through a well-defined series of maturation steps, ultimately giving rise to a myelinating oligodendrocyte (MOL). In mice and humans, it is characterized by the expression of specific molecular markers, including Pdgfra, Cspg4 (also known as NG2) and Olig2.

CL:0000129.label: microglial cell
CL:0000129.description: A transcriptomically distinct central nervous system macrophage found in the parenchyma of the central nervous system. Marker include CD11b-positive, F4/80-positive, and CD68-positive.

CL:0000878.label: central nervous system macrophage
CL:0000878.description: A tissue-resident macrophage found in the central nervous system.

CL:0000130.label: neuron associated cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)

CL:0000131.label: gut endothelial cell
CL:0000131.description: An endothelial cell that lines the blood and lymphatic vessels of the digestive tract. This cell forms the gut–vascular barrier (GVB) through tight junctions and crosstalk with pericytes and enteric glial cells, regulating the passage of nutrients and immune cells while restricting microbial translocation into the bloodstream.

CL:0000223.label: endodermal cell
CL:0000223.description: A cell of the inner of the three germ layers of the embryo.

CL:0000132.label: corneal endothelial cell
CL:0000132.description: An hexagonal, flattened, mitochondria-rich endothelial cell that forms a monolayer on the posterior surface of the cornea (the corneal endothelium). Corneal endothelial cells are derived from the neural crest and are responsible for keeping the cornea transparent by maintaining the tissue in a semi-dry state through the action of their ionic pumps and tight junction barrier.

CL:0000134.label: mesenchymal stem cell
CL:0000134.description: A connective tissue cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses. In humans, this cell type is CD73-positive, CD90-positive, CD105-positive, CD45-negative, CD34-negative, and MHCII-negative. They may further differentiate into osteoblasts, adipocytes, myocytes, neurons, or chondroblasts in vitro. Originally described as residing in the bone marrow, this cell type is now known to reside in many, if not all, adult organs.

CL:0000135.label: fibrocyte
CL:0000135.description: An inactive fibroblast; cytoplasm is sparse, endoplasmic reticulum is scanty with flattened nucleus. Term used by some histologists; when fibroblasts become relatively inactive in fiber formation. However, this cell has the potential for fibrogenesis in quiescent connective tissue of the adult, as well as during development, other histologists prefer to use the term fibroblast in all circumstances. These cells represent ~0.5% of peripheral blood leukocytes.

CL:0000136.label: adipocyte
CL:0000136.description: A fat-storing cell found mostly in the abdominal cavity and subcutaneous tissue of mammals. Fat is usually stored in the form of triglycerides.

CL:0000325.label: stuff accumulating cell
CL:0000325.description: A cell that is specialised to accumulate a particular substance(s).

CL:0000137.label: osteocyte
CL:0000137.description: A mature osteoblast that has become embedded in the bone matrix. They occupy a small cavity, called lacuna, in the matrix and are connected to adjacent osteocytes via protoplasmic projections called canaliculi.

CL:0001040.label: non-terminally differentiated osteoblast
CL:0001040.description: Osteoblast that is non-terminally differentiated and located in cellular bone tissue or under the periosteum in acellular bone.

CL:0000138.label: chondrocyte
CL:0000138.description: Skeletogenic cell that is terminally differentiated, secretes an avascular, GAG-rich matrix, is embedded in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, and develops from a chondroblast cell.

CL:0000667.label: collagen secreting cell
CL:0000667.description: An extracellular matrix secreting cell that secretes collagen.

CL:0000140.label: odontocyte
CL:0000140.description: Skeletogenic cell that secretes dentine matrix, is derived from odontogenic papilla. Embedded in dentine tissue, and is the transformation of a non-terminally differentiated odontoblast cell.

CL:0000141.label: cementocyte
CL:0000141.description: An osteocytelike cell with numerous processes, trapped in a lacuna in the cement of the tooth.

CL:0000142.label: hyalocyte
CL:0000142.description: A cell occurring in the peripheral part of the vitreous body of the eye that may be responsible for production of hyaluronic acid and collagen.

CL:0000144.label: obsolete cell by function
CL:0000144.description: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by their primary end goal or behavior.
comments: This term was made obsolete because there is no difference in meaning between it and 'cell', as any cell can be classified by its function or behavior. If you have used this term in annotation, please replace it with cell (CL:0000000), native cell (CL:0000003), or cell in vitro (CL:0001034) as appropriate.

CL:0000147.label: pigment cell
CL:0000147.description: A pigment cell is a cell that contains pigment granules.

CL:0000148.label: melanocyte
CL:0000148.description: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which gives a brown to black appearance.

CL:0000541.label: melanoblast
CL:0000541.description: A cell that originates from the neural crest and differentiates into a pigment cell.

CL:0000150.label: glandular secretory epithelial cell
CL:0000150.description: An epithelial cell, located in a gland, that is specialised for the synthesis and secretion of specific biomolecules, such as hormones, or mucous.

CL:0000154.label: protein secreting cell
CL:0000154.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some protein secretion.

CL:0000155.label: peptic cell
CL:0000155.description: An epithelial cell of the stomach that is part of the fundic gastric gland. This cell is characterized by a basally located nucleus, abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum, and large apical secretory granules. It produces and secretes pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of the digestive enzyme pepsin.

CL:0002659.label: glandular epithelial cell of stomach
CL:0002659.description: A glandular epithelial cell that is part of the stomach.

CL:0000156.label: obsolete antibody secreting cell
CL:0000156.description: OBSOLETE: A cell of the lymphoid series that can react with antigen to produce specific cell products called antibodies. Various cell subpopulations, often B cells, can be defined, based on the different classes of immunoglobulins that they synthesize.
comments: Consider using 'B cell ; CL:0000236' or one of its children instead.

CL:0000157.label: surfactant secreting cell
CL:0000157.description: A cell that specializes in secretion of surfactant in the alveoli of the lung.

CL:0000158.label: club cell
CL:0000158.description: A non-mucous, epithelial secretory cell that is part of the tracheobronchial tree. A club cell has short microvilli but no cilia. A club cell is able to multiply and differentiate into ciliated cells to regenerate the bronchiolar epithelium and it also protects the tracheobronchial epithelium.

CL:0002202.label: epithelial cell of tracheobronchial tree
CL:0002202.description: An epithelial cell of the tracheobronchial tree.

CL:0008055.label: respiratory tract secretory epithelial cell
CL:0008055.description: A secretory epithelial cell of the respiratory tract epithelium.  These cells have an endodermal origin.

CL:0000160.label: goblet cell
CL:0000160.description: A specialized, columnar, mucus secreting epithelial cell shaped like a flask or goblet. A narrow basal end contains the nucleus while the apical end is swollen by the accumulation of mucus laden secretory granules.  Short microvilli project from the apical plasma membrane.

CL:0000319.label: mucus secreting cell
CL:0000319.description: Any cell that is capable of some mucus secretion.

CL:0000162.label: parietal cell
CL:0000162.description: An epithelial cell of the stomach that is part of the fundic gastric gland. This cell is characterized by its pyramidal shape, abundant mitochondria, and a complex network of secretory canaliculi lined with microvilli. It secretes hydrochloric acid into the stomach lumen and produces intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption.

CL:0000163.label: endocrine cell
CL:0000163.description: A cell of an endocrine gland, ductless glands that secrete substances which are released directly into the circulation and which influence metabolism and other body functions.

CL:0000164.label: enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000164.description: An endocrine cell that is located in the epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract or in the pancreas.

CL:0000165.label: neuroendocrine cell
CL:0000165.description: A neuron that is capable of some hormone secretion in response to neuronal signals.

CL:0000166.label: chromaffin cell
CL:0000166.description: A cell that stores epinephrine secretory vesicles. During times of stress, the nervous system signals the vesicles to secrete their hormonal content. Their name derives from their ability to stain a brownish color with chromic salts. Characteristically, they are located in the adrenal medulla and paraganglia of the sympathetic nervous system.

CL:0000568.label: amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation cell
CL:0000568.description: A cell that originates in the neural crest, that has certain cytochemical and ultrastructural characteristics and is found scattered throughout the body; types include melanocytes, the cells of the chromaffin system, and cells in the hypothalamus, hypophysis, thyroid, parathyroids, lungs, gastrointestinal tract, and pancreas. This cell type concentrates the amino acid precursors of certain amines and decarboxylate them, forming amines that function as regulators and neurotransmitters. This cell type produces substances such as epinephrine, norepinephrine, dopamine, serotonin, enkephalin, somatostatin, neurotensin, and substance P, the actions of which may affect contiguous cells, nearby groups of cells, or distant cells, thus functioning as local or systemic hormones. The name is an acronym for amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation cell.

CL:0000167.label: peptide hormone secreting cell
CL:0000167.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some peptide hormone secretion.

CL:0000168.label: insulin secreting cell
CL:0000168.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some insulin secretion.

CL:0000169.label: type B pancreatic cell
CL:0000169.description: A cell that secretes insulin and is located towards the center of the islets of Langerhans.

CL:0008024.label: pancreatic endocrine cell
CL:0008024.description: An endocrine cell that is part of the pancreas.

CL:0002351.label: progenitor cell of endocrine pancreas
CL:0002351.description: A progenitor cell that is able to differentiate into the pancreas alpha, beta and delta endocrine cells. This cell type expresses neurogenin-3 and Isl-1.

CL:0000171.label: pancreatic A cell
CL:0000171.description: A type A enteroendocrine cell found in the periphery of the islets of Langerhans that secretes glucagon.
synonyms: alpha cell of islet of Langerhans

CL:0002067.label: type A enteroendocrine cell
CL:0002067.description: An enteroendocrine cell that produces glucagon.

CL:0000172.label: somatostatin secreting cell
CL:0000172.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some somatostatin secretion.

CL:0000173.label: pancreatic D cell
CL:0000173.description: A D cell located in the pancreas. Peripherally placed within the islets like type A cells; contains somatostatin.

CL:0000502.label: type D enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000502.description: A cell found throughout the gastrointestinal tract and in the pancreas. They secrete somatostatin in both an endocrine and paracrine manner. Somatostatin inhibits gastrin, cholecystokinin, insulin, glucagon, pancreatic enzymes, and gastric hydrochloric acid. A variety of substances which inhibit gastric acid secretion (vasoactive intestinal peptide, calcitonin gene-related peptide, cholecystokinin, beta-adrenergic agonists, and gastric inhibitory peptide) are thought to act by releasing somatostatin.

CL:0000174.label: steroid hormone secreting cell
CL:0000174.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some steroid hormone secretion.

CL:0000175.label: luteal cell
CL:0000175.description: A progesterone secreting cell in the corpus luteum. The large luteal cells develop from the granulosa cells. The small luteal cells develop from the theca cells.

CL:0000179.label: progesterone secreting cell
CL:0000179.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some progesterone secretion.

CL:0000176.label: ecdysteroid secreting cell
CL:0000176.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some ecdysteroid secretion.

CL:0000177.label: testosterone secreting cell
CL:0000177.description: Any secretory cell that is capable of some testosterone secretion.

CL:0000178.label: Leydig cell
CL:0000178.description: A Leydig cell is a testosterone-secreting cell in the interstitial area, between the seminiferous tubules, in the testis.

CL:4030031.label: interstitial cell
CL:4030031.description: Any cell that is located within the interstitium between the cells most prominent in defining a given tissue. "Interstitial cell" is a morphological term and refers to a variety of cells with differing origins and phenotypes.

CL:0009091.label: Leydig stem cell
CL:0009091.description: A stem cell found in the interstitial compartment of the neonatal testis; it is capable of self-renewal as well as differentiation into steroidogenic cells (adult Leydig cells). Intermediate stages of development include progenitor Leydig cells and immature Leydig cells.

CL:0000180.label: estradiol secreting cell
CL:0000180.description: A steroid hormone secreting cell that secretes estradiol.

CL:0000181.label: obsolete metabolising cell
CL:0000181.description: A cell whose primary function is intermediary metabolism.
comments: Removing this grouping class, because the groupings are incomplete and too hard to maintain.

CL:0000182.label: hepatocyte
CL:0000182.description: The main structural component of the liver. They are specialized epithelial cells that are organized into interconnected plates called lobules. Majority of cell population of liver, polygonal in shape, arranged in plates or trabeculae between sinusoids; may have single nucleus or binucleated.

CL:0005026.label: hepatoblast
CL:0005026.description: Multi fate stem cell that gives rise to both hepatocytes and cholangiocytes as descendants. The term often refers to fetal precursors of hepatocytes (differently from 'hepatic stem cell', usually applied to the self-renewing pool of hepatocyte precursors in the adult liver). Hepatoblasts may also be endogenous, as some stem cells found in the liver come from the bone marrow via blood circulation.

CL:0000183.label: contractile cell
CL:0000183.description: A cell whose primary function is to shorten.

CL:0000669.label: pericyte
CL:0000669.description: An elongated, contractile cell found wrapped about precapillary arterioles outside the basement membrane. Pericytes are present in capillaries where proper adventitia and muscle layer are missing (thus distingushing this cell type from adventitial cells). They are relatively undifferentiated and may become fibroblasts, macrophages, or smooth muscle cells.

CL:0000185.label: myoepithelial cell
CL:0000185.description: Contractile cells resembling smooth muscle cells that are present in glands, notably the mammary gland, and aid in secretion. This cell has long weaving dendritic processes containing myofilament.

CL:0000186.label: myofibroblast cell
CL:0000186.description: An animal cell that has characteristics of both a fibroblast cell and a smooth muscle cell.

CL:0000187.label: muscle cell
CL:0000187.description: A mature contractile cell, commonly known as a myocyte. This cell has as part of its cytoplasm myofibrils organized in various patterns.

CL:0000393.label: electrically responsive cell
CL:0000393.description: A cell whose function is determined by its response to an electric signal.

CL:0000188.label: cell of skeletal muscle
CL:0000188.description: A somatic cell located in skeletal muscle.

CL:0000189.label: slow muscle cell
CL:0000189.description: A muscle cell that develops tension more slowly than a fast-twitch fiber.

CL:0008046.label: extrafusal muscle fiber
CL:0008046.description: A skeletal muscle fiber that is innervated by alpha motor neuron and generates tension by contracting, thereby allowing for skeletal movement. These fibers make up the large mass of skeletal muscle tissue and are attached to bones by tendons.

CL:0000857.label: slow muscle myoblast
CL:0000857.description: A skeletal muscle myoblast that differentiates into slow muscle fibers.

CL:0000190.label: fast muscle cell
CL:0000190.description: A muscle cell that can develop high tension rapidly. It is usually innervated by a single alpha neuron.

CL:0000858.label: fast muscle myoblast
CL:0000858.description: A skeletal muscle myoblast that differentiates into fast muscle fibers.

CL:0008000.label: non-striated muscle cell
CL:0008000.description: Any muscle cell in which the fibers are not organised into sarcomeres.

CL:0008007.label: visceral muscle cell
CL:0008007.description: A muscle cell that is part of some visceral muscle.

CL:0000514.label: smooth muscle myoblast
CL:0000514.description: A precursor cell destined to differentiate into smooth muscle myocytes.

CL:0000193.label: cardiac muscle cell (sensu Arthopoda)
CL:0000193.description: A striated muscle cell of an arthropod heart that participates in heart contraction.

CL:0000465.label: cardioblast (sensu Arthropoda)
CL:0000465.description: A precursor of the cells that form the dorsal vessel of arthropods.

CL:0000746.label: cardiac muscle cell
CL:0000746.description: Cardiac muscle cells are striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction. In mammals, the contractile fiber resembles those of skeletal muscle but are only one third as large in diameter, are richer in sarcoplasm, and contain centrally located instead of peripheral nuclei.

CL:0000194.label: obsolete nodal cardiac cell
comments: Consider CL:0002072.

CL:0000196.label: insect flight muscle cell
CL:0000196.description: A muscle cell that is involved in the mechanism of insect flight. This encompasses both, cells that power flight and cells that control flight.

CL:0008003.label: somatic muscle myotube
CL:0008003.description: A myotube that is part of some somatic muscle.  Examples include arthropod somatic muscle cells.

CL:0000198.label: pain receptor cell
CL:0000198.description: The peripheral receptor for pain. Includes receptors which are sensitive to painful mechanical stimuli, extreme heat or cold, and chemical stimuli. All mammalian nociceptors are free nerve endings.

CL:0000199.label: mechanoreceptor cell
CL:0000199.description: A cell specialized to transduce mechanical stimuli and relay that information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000200.label: touch receptor cell
CL:0000200.description: Any neuron that is capable of some detection of mechanical stimulus involved in sensory perception of touch.

CL:0000202.label: auditory hair cell
CL:0000202.description: A mechanoreceptor cell of the auditory or vestibular system that is sensitive to auditory stimuli. The accessory sensory structures are arranged so that appropriate stimuli cause movement of the hair-like projections (stereocilia and kinocilia) which relay the information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000855.label: sensory hair cell
CL:0000855.description: Hair cell is a mechanoreceptor cell that is sensitive to movement of the hair-like projections (stereocilia and kinocilia) which relay the information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000203.label: gravity sensitive cell
CL:0000203.description: Any neuronal receptor cell that is capable of some detection of mechanical stimulus involved in sensory perception of gravity.

CL:0000205.label: thermoreceptor cell
CL:0000205.description: A cellular receptor which mediates the sense of temperature. Thermoreceptor cells in vertebrates are mostly located under the skin. In mammals there are separate types of thermoreceptors for cold and for warmth and pain receptor cells which detect cold or heat extreme enough to cause pain.

CL:0000206.label: chemoreceptor cell
CL:0000206.description: A cell specialized to detect chemical substances and relay that information centrally in the nervous system. Chemoreceptors may monitor external stimuli, as in taste and olfaction, or internal stimuli, such as the concentrations of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the blood.

CL:0000207.label: olfactory receptor cell
CL:0000207.description: Any neuron that is capable of some detection of chemical stimulus involved in sensory perception of smell.

CL:0000209.label: taste receptor cell
CL:0000209.description: A specialized cell involved in gustatory sensory perception.

CL:0000210.label: photoreceptor cell
CL:0000210.description: A cell specialized in detecting light stimuli that are involved in visual perception.

CL:0000211.label: electrically active cell
CL:0000211.description: A cell whose function is determined by the generation or the reception of an electric signal.

CL:0000212.label: obsolete absorptive cell
CL:0000212.description: OBSOLETE. A cell that takes up and metabolizes substances.
comments: It has no child terms. Consider using 'gut absorptive cell'.

CL:0000213.label: obsolete lining cell
CL:0000213.description: OBSOLETE. A cell within an epithelial cell sheet whose main function is to act as an internal or external covering for a tissue or an organism.
comments: Obsoleted term because redundant

CL:0000214.label: synovial cell
CL:0000214.description: A cell located in the synovial joint.

CL:0000216.label: Sertoli cell
CL:0000216.description: A supporting cell projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules. They surround and nourish the developing male germ cells and secrete androgen binding protein. Their tight junctions with the spermatogonia and spermatocytes provide a blood-testis barrier.

CL:0000630.label: supporting cell
CL:0000630.description: A cell whose primary function is to support other cell types.

CL:0000511.label: androgen binding protein secreting cell
CL:0000511.description: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes androgen binding protein.

CL:0002625.label: seminiferous tubule epithelial cell
CL:0002625.description: A cell of the seminiferous tubule epithelium.

CL:0000217.label: obsolete insulating cell
comments: obsoleted because the term is not needed

CL:0000218.label: myelinating Schwann cell
CL:0000218.description: A neuroglial cell of the peripheral nervous system which forms the insulating myelin sheaths of peripheral axons.

CL:0002573.label: Schwann cell
CL:0002573.description: A glial cell that myelinates or ensheathes axons in the peripheral nervous system.

CL:0002377.label: immature Schwann cell
CL:0002377.description: A glial cell that develops from a Schwann cell precursor. The immature Schwann cell is embedded among neurons (axons) with minimal extracellular spaces separating them from nerve cell membranes and has a basal lamina. Cells can survive without an axon present. Immature Schwann cell can be found communally ensheathing large groups of axons.

CL:0000219.label: motile cell
CL:0000219.description: A cell that moves by its own activities.

CL:0000220.label: obsolete cell by lineage
comments: This term was made obsolete because there is no difference in meaning between it and 'cell', as any cell in a multicellular organiam, apart from a zygote, can potentially be classified by its lineage. If you have used this term in annotation, please replace it with cell (CL:0000000), native cell (CL:0000003), or cell in vitro (CL:0001034) as appropriate.

CL:0000224.label: obsolete cell by nuclear number
CL:0000224.description: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by the number of their nuclei.
comments: This term was made obsolete because there is no difference in meaning between it and 'cell', as any cell can be classified by its nuclear number (note that this term was previously used as a parent class of enucleate cell). If you have used this term in annotation, please replace it with cell (CL:0000000), native cell (CL:0000003), or cell in vitro (CL:0001034) as appropriate.

CL:0000225.label: anucleate cell
CL:0000225.description: A cell that lacks a nucleus.

CL:0002242.label: nucleate cell
CL:0002242.description: A cell containing at least one nucleus.

CL:0000226.label: single nucleate cell
CL:0000226.description: A cell with a single nucleus.

CL:0000227.label: binucleate cell
CL:0000227.description: Any cell that has characteristic some binucleate.

CL:0000228.label: multinucleate cell
CL:0000228.description: A cell with more than one nucleus.

CL:0000229.label: obsolete lymphoblast
CL:0000229.description: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).
comments: Refers to an activated mature lymphocyte phenotype rather than a distinct cell type; consider using 'lymphocyte ; CL:0000542' or one of its children instead.

CL:0000230.label: obsolete T lymphoblast
CL:0000230.description: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).
comments: Refers to an activated mature T lymphocyte phenotype rather than a distinct cell type; consider using 'T cell ; CL:0000084' or one of its children instead.

CL:0000231.label: obsolete B lymphoblast
CL:0000231.description: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).
comments: Refers to an activated mature B lymphocyte phenotype rather than a distinct cell type; consider using 'B cell ; CL:0000236' or one of its children instead.

CL:0000232.label: erythrocyte
CL:0000232.description: A red blood cell. In mammals, mature erythrocytes are biconcave disks containing hemoglobin whose function is to transport oxygen.

CL:0000329.label: oxygen accumulating cell
CL:0000329.description: Any cell that is capable of some oxygen transport.

CL:0000558.label: reticulocyte
CL:0000558.description: An immature erythrocyte that changes the protein composition of its plasma membrane by exosome formation and extrusion. The types of protein removed differ between species though removal of the transferrin receptor is apparent in mammals and birds.

CL:0000233.label: platelet
CL:0000233.description: A non-nucleated disk-shaped cell formed by extrusion from megakaryocytes, found in the blood of all mammals, and mainly involved in blood coagulation.

CL:0000556.label: megakaryocyte
CL:0000556.description: A large hematopoietic cell (50 to 100 micron) with a lobated nucleus. Once mature, this cell undergoes multiple rounds of endomitosis and cytoplasmic restructuring to allow platelet formation and release.

CL:0000235.label: macrophage
CL:0000235.description: A mononuclear phagocyte present in variety of tissues, typically differentiated from monocytes, capable of phagocytosing a variety of extracellular particulate material, including immune complexes, microorganisms, and dead cells.

CL:0000236.label: B cell
CL:0000236.description: A lymphocyte of B lineage that is capable of B cell mediated immunity.

CL:0000240.label: stratified squamous epithelial cell
CL:0000240.description: A stratified epithelial cell that is part of squamous epithelium, characterized by multiple layers of cells. The basal layer is directly attached to the basement membrane and the apical layer consists of flattened squamous cells. This provides a protective barrier, commonly found in areas subject to abrasion, such as the skin, oral cavity, and esophagus.

CL:0000239.label: brush border epithelial cell
CL:0000239.description: An epithelial cell characterized by the presence of a brush border on its apical surface, which increases the surface area for absorption.

CL:0000241.label: stratified cuboidal epithelial cell
CL:0000241.description: A stratified epithelial cell that is part of cuboidal epithelium, characterized by multiple layers of cuboidal cells forming the apical layer. This provides a protective lining for ducts in large glands, such as sweat glands.

CL:0000242.label: Merkel cell
CL:0000242.description: A specialized epithelial cell located in the skin epidermis and certain mucosal epithelia. It functions as a mechanoreceptor for light touch by forming synapse-like contacts with somatosensory afferent nerve endings, contributing to slowly adapting type I (SAI) tactile responses. Characterized by dense-core neuroendocrine granules, the Merkel cell exhibits both sensory and neuroendocrine properties, including regulated neurotransmitter release via SNARE complex-dependent mechanisms. Its development in mice depends on the transcription factor Atoh1.

CL:0000243.label: obsolete glial cell (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000243.description: A non-neuronal cell of the nervous system. They not only provide physical support, but also respond to injury, regulate the ionic and chemical composition of the extracellular milieu. Form the myelin insulation of nervous pathways, guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons. Neuroglia have high-affinity transmitter uptake systems, voltage-dependent and transmitter-gated ion channels, and can release transmitters, but their role in signaling (as in many other functions) is unclear.
comments: This is a grouping class that is no longer needed or wanted.

CL:0000244.label: transitional epithelial cell
CL:0000244.description: A cell characteristically found lining hollow organs that are subject to great mechanical change due to contraction and distention; originally thought to represent a transition between stratified squamous and columnar epithelium.

CL:0000245.label: obsolete passage cell
CL:0000245.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000353 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell in exodermis or endodermis that remains thin walled when the associated cells develop thick secondary walls. Has casparian strip in endodermis.

CL:0000247.label: Rohon-Beard neuron
CL:0000247.description: Type of neuron that is a primary mechanosensory cell, with peripheral neurites innervating the skin with free nerve endings.

CL:0000531.label: primary sensory neuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000531.description: A primary neuron (sensu Teleostei) that has a sensory function.

CL:0000248.label: obsolete microsporocyte
CL:0000248.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0020047 from Plant Ontology instead. A diploid (2n) cell that undergoes meiosis and forms four haploid (1n) microspores; also called microspore mother cell and, in seed plants, pollen mother cell.

CL:0000250.label: obsolete megaspore
CL:0000250.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0020019 from Plant Ontology instead. A haploid (1n) spore developing into a female gametophyte in heterosporous plants.

CL:0000252.label: obsolete microspore
CL:0000252.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0020048 from Plant Ontology instead. A haploid (1n) spore developing into a male gametophyte in heterosporous plants; the uninucleate pollen grain in seed plants.

CL:0000254.label: obsolete egg cell
CL:0000254.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0020094 from Plant Ontology instead. The female gamete of plants.

CL:0000257.label: Eumycetozoan cell
CL:0000257.description: Any cell that in taxon some Eumycetozoa.

CL:0000258.label: obsolete fiber tracheid
CL:0000258.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000355 from Plant Ontology instead. A fiber like tracheid in the secondary xylem; commonly thick walled, with pointed ends and bordered pits that have lenticular to slit like apertures.

CL:0000260.label: obsolete mucilage cell
CL:0000260.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000373 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell containing mucilages or gums or similar carbohydrate material characterized by the property of swelling in water.

CL:0000261.label: obsolete anterior cell
comments: Obsoleted becuase this term has an overly general name, no definition, and by it's classification appears to refer to a very specific cell type in dictystelium.  If needed, the term should be in DDANAT - probably as a subclass of http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DDANAT_0000002

CL:0000262.label: obsolete guard mother cell
CL:0000262.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000351 from Plant Ontology instead. An epidermal cell that divides to produce the guard cells.

CL:0000264.label: obsolete phloem initial
CL:0000264.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000400 from Plant Ontology instead. A cambial cell on the phloem side of the cambial zone that is the source of one or more cells arising by periclinal divisions and differentiating into phloem elements with or without additional divisions in various planes.

CL:0000266.label: obsolete meristemoid
CL:0000266.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0004011 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell constituting an active locus of meristematic activity in a tissue composed of somewhat older, differentiating cells.

CL:0000268.label: obsolete sieve element
CL:0000268.description: Obsolete. Consult Plant Ontology instead. The cell in the phloem tissue concerned with mainly longitudinal conduction of food materials. Classified into sieve cell and sieve tube member.

CL:0000270.label: obsolete subsidiary cell
CL:0000270.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000284 from Plant Ontology instead. An epidermal cell associated with a stoma and at least morphologically distinguishable from the epidermal cells composing the groundmass of the tissue.

CL:0000272.label: obsolete cambial initial
CL:0000272.description: OBSOLETE, use term from Plant Ontology. A cell localized in the vascular cambium or phellogen. Its periclinal division can contribute cells either to the outside or to the inside of the axis; in vascular cambium, classified into fusiform initials (source of axial cells of xylem and phloem) and ray initials (source of the ray cells).
comments: replaced_by PO:0000295

CL:0000276.label: obsolete sclerenchyma cell
CL:0000276.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000077 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell variable in form and size, being more or less thick, often lignified, secondary walls. Belongs to the category of subcells and may or may not be devoid of protoplast at maturity.

CL:0000277.label: obsolete prestalk I cell
CL:0000277.description: OBSOLETE: Initial population of prestalk cells that activate the ecmA promoter at the mound stage and that presumably further differentiate into pstA and pstO cells.
comments: This cell type does not exist in Dictyostelium. it has been long deleted in their anatomy ontology.

CL:0000278.label: obsolete central cell
CL:0000278.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0020090 from Plant Ontology instead. OBSOLETED, use term from Plant Ontology. A cell containing the two polar nuclei which, after double fertilization, will develop into the endosperm.

CL:0000280.label: obsolete generative cell
CL:0000280.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0020097 from Plant Ontology instead. The cell that will give rise to the generative nuclei which will participate in fertilization.

CL:0000282.label: obsolete trichome
CL:0000282.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000282 from Plant Ontology instead. An outgrowth from the epidermis. Trichomes vary in size and complexity and include hairs, scales, and other structures and may be glandular. In Arabidopsis, patterning of trichome development is not random but does not appear to be lineage-based like stomata.

CL:0000284.label: obsolete companion cell
CL:0000284.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000071 from Plant Ontology instead. A specialized parenchyma cell associated with a sieve-tube member in angiosperm phloem and arising from the same mother cell as the sieve-tube member.

CL:0000286.label: hyphal cell
CL:0000286.description: A cell of a filament of a fungal mycelium.

CL:0000521.label: fungal cell
CL:0000521.description: Any cell that in taxon some Fungi.

CL:0000287.label: eye photoreceptor cell
CL:0000287.description: Any photoreceptor cell that is part of some eye.

CL:0000288.label: obsolete synergid
CL:0000288.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000191 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell in the micropylar end of the embryo sac associated with the egg in the egg apparatus of angiosperms. Plays a vital role in fertilization.

CL:0000290.label: obsolete xylem fiber cell
CL:0000290.description: Obsolete. Use PO:0000274 from Plant Ontology instead. A fiber of the xylem tissue, Two types are recognized in the secondary xylem: fiber tracheids and libriform fibers.

CL:0000292.label: obsolete guard cell
